changes_since_the_proof_audit_edition.summary: The A076227 attribution. Section 1 gains two paragraphs stating that the word counts used here are Collatz word counts -- the shortcut Collatz map moves log x by -log 2 or +log(3/2) and the Juggler map moves log log n by the same two steps, so a word contracts in one problem exactly when it contracts in the other -- naming A076227 for the survivor counts, A100982 for the minimal certificates and A020914 for their admissible lengths, disclaiming priority for all three, and locating the contribution where the two problems part: Terras's bijection makes the fair-share densities free for Collatz, while for the Juggler map they are Hypothesis FD. Lemma 5.1 is labelled as verifying the first terms of A100982 rather than establishing them. Remark 6.2 notes that the decay it proves is a statement about Collatz residue classes as well. The Section 8 evidence table gains a row for the shared word counts. References 5 to 7 are the three OEIS entries. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed; Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are untouched. THE PSI SCOPE QUESTION, settled in this edition. Section 6 previously said that whether Winkler's normalized oscillations for A100982 determine this paper's psi was a question about the identity M_d = 2 N_(d-1) - N_d and had not been checked. Section 7 of that preprint has now been read. Corollary 11 gives only a root limit with no rate, and Corollary 12 proves that r a_3(r) divided by its lower cycle bound has liminf 1 and limsup alpha/(alpha-1) = 2.7095112914 for alpha = log2 3, the lower value attained exactly on the record minima of frac(r alpha) and the sup approached along the record maxima. That is an exact statement about the extremes of two sparse sets of orders and not an asymptotic for a general r, so it carries no error term and does not transmit through the tail. The envelope is a factor 2.71 wide while the whole oscillation of psi spans 1.06, some twenty-eight times narrower. Section 6 therefore claims psi and cites Winkler for the bound, where it previously withheld the claim. Reference 13 records both corollaries. Both were verified against this paper's own counts in tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_winkler_envelope.py. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed; Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are untouched. THE DROPPING-TIME NAME, added in this edition. Section 1 already credited A076227, A100982 and A020914 and disclaimed priority, but described A020914 by its construction, 'the binary lengths of the powers of three'. The Collatz literature indexes it by what it means: A020914 is the set of allowable DROPPING TIMES of the shortcut map, recorded as such in its OEIS entry since 22 October 2009, with the dropping time of an individual start tabulated as A126241. The length of a minimal certificate is a dropping time. Verified in the laboratory before the sentence was written, three ways in exact integer arithmetic: the lengths carrying a minimal certificate are A020914 over d <= 21; every n in [3, 20000) has its parity word to its dropping time a minimal certificate, zero failures; every dropping time attained below 2e6 lies in A020914, no exception. Nothing mathematical changes and no claim is withdrawn. A referee was being told the construction rather than the name, and the name is the one the field indexes on. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed. VOCABULARY COLLISION DECLARED, same day, after a peer followed the cross-references. The attribution sentence said A076227 counts the residue classes on which the Collatz STOPPING time is not constant. In OEIS vocabulary that is the wrong quantity: A076227's own comment names A074473, titled 'Dropping time for the 3x+1 problem', while OEIS reserves stopping time for the steps needed to reach 1 (A006666 counts the halving steps). The paper is not simply wrong -- Terras, whom it follows, calls the first fall below the start the stopping time -- but it had declared neither convention, and after the dropping-time addition earlier today it used both in one paragraph. Section 1 now uses the OEIS term in the attribution, since that is what is being attributed, and adds a sentence naming both conventions and saying they are one object. The keyword list follows. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed. 2026-09-20 REVISION, ONE PARAGRAPH AND ONE REFERENCE: the exponential rate is attributed to Lagarias, Theorem D of reference [14], which the previous edition did not cite at all. That edition said the rate 'is not folklore' and credited Hikawa [9, Section 6], repeating his remark that it appears to be new for these sequences. The rate is Theorem D's eta and has been in print since 1985; the link is an identity, 2^(-eta) = 2^(H(p)-1) = p^(-p)(1-p)^(p-1)/2 = vartheta(p), verified to fifty digits. Hikawa Section 6 is now described as an independent proof in the weight basis whose constants are eta rescaled, and his novelty remark is marked incorrect. What is still his is the weight-basis form and Conjecture 7.1; nothing else in the manuscript changed, and the page count is unchanged at 41. THE VERSION STAMP AND THE RENDERED PDF HAVE NOT BEEN REVIEWED BY THE AUTHOR. 2026-09-20 SECOND EDITION OF THE DAY, revised in the evening after the morning's Lagarias attribution. Section 1 names the third name of the minimal certificate length, the glide, and cites Hikawa's toolkit, whose survivor counts, minimal-certificate counts and odd-count refinement were run and agree with the counts used here. Section 5 records that Lemma 5.1 and its extension to every length, the five-step partition behind Theorem 5.4 and the assembly of the count are machine-checked, and that length six adds no minimal certificate while length seven adds exactly three. Section 6 repairs one symbol carrying two meanings -- M_d was both the survivors on the barrier of the recursion and the minimal-certificate count in the Winkler paragraph; the latter is now written 2N_(d-1) - N_d = b_(d-1) M_(d-1) -- cites T. D. Noe's 2011 tabulation of the certificate-density increments on A186008 and the nonzero counts on A186009, states the reading status of the parity-vector preprints as the registry records it (Nakanishi's Jxiv paper read in full; of the January preprint only the abstract; of the July preprint the author's version note, from which its Sections 6 and 7 are cited; the September preprint listed as reference 17 with nothing of its text available), and replaces the differenced jump sum 4.58 and its steepening power law with the closed forms: the jump of psi at frac(n beta) is a_1 N_n / (2 rho)^(n-1), reproduced to 2.3e-14 over n <= 3000 by a transfer-operator propagation, with a_1 = 1/(2 rho sqrt(2 pi beta (1 - beta))) = 0.427956804, the Fourier identity psihat(k) = Phihat(k) G(e^(-2 pi i k beta)) with the ladder profile Phi in closed form, and the mean kappa G(1) = 10.8927. Section 8's evidence table gains rows for the prefactor (verified computation, existence of the limit not proved) and for the machine-checked finite combinatorics, and its Lean paragraph now lists the twelve modules with the declarations audited for each; formal/AxiomCheckPaperBPublished.lean grew from eight to twenty-nine declarations to back that list, all kernel-checked with no native_decide, while the manuscript still claims no formalization of the analytic estimates. References 15 to 17 added; the annotations of 9 and 10 now say what was read. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof of Sections 2-4, 7 or the appendices changed; Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are untouched. The version stamp is 20 September 2026; the source and PDF were built by the agent and READ PAGE BY PAGE BY THE AGENT ON THE CHANGED PAGES, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE AUTHOR. THIRD BUILD OF THE DAY. Both Hikawa preprints read in full from the author's PDFs supplied by Philippe: the July paper (reference 9, v2.1 of 2 August 2026, 47 pages) and the September paper (reference 17, 57 pages). Section 6 now cites the rate as Theorem 6.3 of the July text and Theorem 7.3 of the September one, Remark 6.5 for the length-basis form, Remark 6.6 for the claim that no asymptotic formula existed, Table 3 / Table 4 for the d^(-3/2) residual (all four rows recompute exactly from the laboratory's counts; tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_hikawa_tables.py), equation (48) of the September text as the count identity in the weight indexing, and, in the priority paragraph, the one sentence of the July text's Section 7.3 that attributes the bounded fluctuation of the residual to the fractional part of lambda d: the novelty claim for the prefactor is narrowed to the function, its measurement and the barrier-step mechanism, and no longer to the suspicion that the phase matters. The reference annotations for 9, 10 and 17 say what each text contains. No theorem, constant or proof changed.
